function: Reads each unit's assembled document (document/L0X.md) before it is accepted, and asserts that every child-facing section body is rendered prose rather than serialized source data. Concretely: for each section named in unit_prose.v1.md (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate, Identification, Troubleshooting, Adult safety verification), attempt json.loads on the section body and fail the unit if it parses; additionally assert every rendered fact resolves to a pointer in the unit's own domain block and that the rendered string equals what is there. Emits a per-section pass/fail list plus the offending line range, and blocks acceptance of the unit. Deterministic, no model invocation.
what_makes_it_sota: Yin Li's OrderBench study (arXiv:2607.18261) measures the exact failure this closes: across 2,400 calls, Gemma-2-2B produced 100% schema-valid output at 2% semantic success with 41.7% unsafe acceptance, and Qwen3-30B-A3B 100% schema-valid at ~31% semantic success, concluding that 'schema validity can be perfect while semantic reliability remains insufficient for direct execution' and prescribing a distinct downstream verification layer. LLMStructBench (arXiv:2604.25359) reproduces the persistence of semantic error under structural validity across models and prompting strategies. Waxell's production writeup places exactly this check first in a three-layer architecture -- 'Before any LLM judgment, run structural validation on the output' -- because deterministic checks 'catch a large category of failures - structured output failures, format errors, and obvious hallucinations' and because a same-family judge 'inherits the same blind spots'. The evidence-driven release-gate study (arXiv:2603.15676) shows why this must be its own reported dimension: across 38 evaluation runs, both ROLLBACK decisions were triggered by a specific coverage dimension rather than by an aggregate score.
role_in_curriculum_builder: New deterministic unit-stage check, run at gate 2 immediately after document assembly and before any unit is written to results/unit_checks.json -- i.e. before RECEIPT-HASH-RESOLVES and before any reviewer stage. It is the execution of DOC-DERIVED-FROM-SOURCE, which policy/checks.v1.yaml already defines but which produced no result for this run: the run root holds only gate_0_logger.json and gate_1_static_preflight.json, with no gate-2 deterministic results file at all.
issues_resolved: The QA report's top Critical: 'Document renderer dumps raw JSON as lesson body. All 4 lessons (L01-L04). Sections under Engage/Explore/Explain/... contain literal structured objects instead of prose' -- visible at L01/document/L01.md:15-19 and identically in L02-L04, which the report attributes to a 'Single templating bug, not four independent failures'. A json.loads on the first section of L01 would have failed the very first unit instead of letting the bug repeat across all four.

function: Runs exactly one judge invocation per unit per pass, from a model family different to the generator's, with an explicit rubric and randomised presentation order. Scores per named dimension -- prose rendering, readability band, vocabulary cap, Bloom alignment, domain-fact plausibility, safety-block completeness -- and emits one verdict per dimension with its rationale rather than a single holistic accept/reject. Its own agreement with a human rater is measured on a held-out sample before its verdicts are treated as gating, and that agreement figure is recorded alongside them.
what_makes_it_sota: Yang et al. (arXiv:2604.22891) evaluate 20 mainstream LLMs on self-preference bias and find '17 of the 20 models reach significance', with advanced capability 'often uncorrelated, or even negatively correlated, with low SPB' -- so a different model *family* is required, not merely a different instance. The same paper measures a 31.5% average bias reduction from forcing structured multi-dimensional evaluation over a single holistic score, which is why this agent emits per-dimension verdicts. 'Judging with Many Minds' (arXiv:2505.19477) shows multi-agent panels can amplify shared blind spots as readily as resist them, supporting one well-chosen judge over a restored panel. Genii (arXiv:2510.08145) shows judge bias can be mitigated without human-labelled data, 'even when weaker models act as server agents', which matters for a project with no rated corpus. Nubank's 100M-user deployment (arXiv:2606.08867) treats 'rigorous LLM judge evaluation with measured inter-rater agreement' as a pillar of the framework, which is where the human-agreement requirement comes from.
role_in_curriculum_builder: Un-defers and replaces the bypassed REV-JUDGE-SINGLE-CROSS-FAMILY at the golden/reviewers stage in policy/checks.v1.yaml (currently marked deferred: RT-5). It runs after the Rendering Conformance Gate and after the deterministic calibration checks, so that it never spends its single invocation on a document that a deterministic check would have rejected.
issues_resolved: acceptance.json for all four units records 'routing_divergence: USER_AUTHORIZED_IN_SESSION_MODEL; cross-family judge bypassed', which the QA report escalates as Critical: 'The one subjective quality check was bypassed identically on all 4 units... REV-JUDGE-SINGLE-CROSS-FAMILY -- the only check that reads output like a human would -- never ran.' The authoring model was the only model that ever saw its own output for the entire run.

agent: Calibration Compliance Checker (readability, vocabulary, Bloom verbs)
function: Reads the rendered document, not workers/lab.json, and emits three independent measurements: (a) the Flesch-Kincaid score against the band declared in policy/calibration.v1.yaml, reported as a band violation in either direction; (b) every term appearing in the rendered prose that is not in the unit's declared vocabulary list and carries no child_definition in the rendered text, listed by name and counted against the declared cap; (c) each objective's opening verb against the ordered bloom_verbs table, reporting every disagreement with the declared bloom_level. (a) and (b) block; (c) flags and never blocks.
what_makes_it_sota: ReadCtrl (arXiv:2406.09205) shows readability-controlled generation and verification substantially beats plain prompting at hitting a target band, with 'a win rate of 52.1%:35.7% against GPT-4 in human evaluations' -- so a checked band outperforms a prompted one. The CEFR study of Rabih, Qwaider & Briscoe (arXiv:2606.21981) shows a single aggregate readability score is insufficient and that compliance needs multi-dimensional structural and lexical checking, which is why vocabulary is measured separately from grade level rather than folded into one number (cited for its methodology only: its domain is Arabic CEFR, not English grade bands). Scaria, Chenna & Subramani (arXiv:2408.04394) find LLMs can hit targeted Bloom levels with good prompting but state 'automated evaluation is not on par with human evaluation', which is direct external support for the flag-never-block posture policy/checks.v1.yaml already specifies for TEXT-BLOOM-VERBS on the grounds that human raters agree only 46.58% of the time. SciEval (arXiv:2604.25472) scores instructional materials 'across 13 criteria (N=3549) using the EQuIP rubric' and finds that of mainstream LLMs 'none achieve strong performance', bounding how much of this should be delegated to a model at all.
role_in_curriculum_builder: Executes TEXT-READABILITY-BAND and TEXT-BLOOM-VERBS -- both defined under the unit group in policy/checks.v1.yaml and neither present in results/unit_checks.json for any of L01-L04 -- at gate 2, immediately after the Rendering Conformance Gate. The ordering is load-bearing: run against this run's output as it stands, the readability score would have been computed over JSON punctuation and would have been meaningless.
issues_resolved: Two findings. The QA report's Critical: 'Readability/quality gates never ran... No TEXT-READABILITY-BAND, no TEXT-BLOOM-VERBS, despite prompt.md naming both as mandatory gate-2 checks run on every unit in every subject.' And its High: 'Vocabulary cap violated where prose exists at all... L04 (document/L04.md:26-27,59,89): mAVohm, 10A socket, mode dial, fuse -- 4+ undefined terms against a cap of 2', with L01's child_definition for 'rail' existing 'only in workers/lab.json, never surfaces in document text'. Reading the four documents directly adds a third: all twelve objectives across L01-L04 open with point to / explain / trace, a flat cognitive demand across the whole sequence that the declared-field check LAB-BLOOM-DEPTH cannot see.

function: Checks each specific physical claim in the rendered lesson -- multimeter socket and fuse behaviour, breadboard clip and trench topology, power-rail continuity caveats -- against the frozen domain reference the run already carries under inputs/ and sources/. Scores a factual-accuracy dimension, and on failure returns targeted feedback into a regeneration pass for the offending claim rather than emitting a bare rejection of the unit. Any claim with no supporting pointer in the domain reference is reported as ungrounded rather than assumed correct.
what_makes_it_sota: arXiv:2607.18261 establishes that schema-constrained generation gives no protection against domain-level falsehood (100% schema validity at 2-31% semantic success) and prescribes domain verification as a distinct downstream layer with fail-closed execution. The K-12 XR pipeline (arXiv:2604.04728) implements precisely this pattern in production form: a Safeguard Agent scoring content against five named criteria -- age-appropriateness, accuracy (factual content), safety, bias, educational value -- where 'If the output fails the review, the pipeline re-enters the generation stage, using safeguard feedback to guide the next attempt', a generation-revision loop rather than accept/reject. Chu et al.'s educational-agent survey (arXiv:2503.11733) treats content generation and error/fact detection as distinct specialised agent roles rather than one generic reviewer, which is why this reads the domain reference that the general judge does not.
role_in_curriculum_builder: New reviewer-stage agent in policy/checks.v1.yaml, running after the Rendering Conformance Gate and before the Cross-Family Structured Judge, taking the rendered document plus the unit's frozen domain_seed.json and sources/ as input. It sits beside DOMAIN-VERIFIER, which validates the domain block's shape; this one validates the truth of what was rendered from it.
issues_resolved: L04/document/L04.md:89 asserts 'The mAVohm socket shares one small fuse across voltage, resistance, and currents under 200 mA; a separate 10A socket exists so a larger expected current does not risk that same fuse' -- a specific claim about meter protection topology, taught to a nine-year-old in a lab about socket selection, that no executed check verifies. The QA report's own root-cause framing covers the gap: '100% schema validity has been measured alongside 2.0% semantic success. A valid unit is a shaped unit, not a correct one.'

function: Walks the rendered numbered Explore steps as if performing the lab, then checks the Adult safety verification block against them: every location or action named in endpoint_check appears in the numbered steps above it; the declared hazard_mode matches what the steps actually ask the child to do; no step implies contact with an energized or connected part that the stated limits forbid; and the block is legible prose that the signing adult can act on. Emits a per-assertion verdict on a named safety dimension with authority to block acceptance.
what_makes_it_sota: NSTA's Science Activity Safety Checklist (Kenneth Roy, 2018) sets the professional standard as a rehearsal rather than a document review -- perform the activity yourself before using it with students -- alongside documented physical-hazard and hand/power-tool precautions and a written safety-precautions statement, which maps onto an agent that walks the steps rather than checking that JSON fields are present. The K-12 Safeguard Agent pattern (arXiv:2604.04728) already implements named-dimension safety scoring with a generation-revision loop, directly transferable to a hands-on-hardware dimension. Sadhu & Dhor's hierarchical adversarial oversight framework (arXiv:2512.22496) supports making physical safety its own review layer with its own authority rather than one line in a general judge's rubric, since a general quality judge has no particular reason to prioritise an unreadable safety block over a dull hook.
role_in_curriculum_builder: New reviewer-stage agent, running on every unit whose adult_verification block sets signoff_required: true -- which is all four units in this run -- after the Rendering Conformance Gate and in parallel with the Domain-Fact Safeguard Reviewer. Its verdict is recorded in the unit's acceptance.json alongside the routing decision, so a bypass of it is visible in the same place the judge bypass was.
issues_resolved: The Adult safety verification block, which is the sole mechanism by which an adult is expected to confirm 'Battery lead visibly separated from the module; no jumper connects a source to a rail' (L01/document/L01.md:163-173), shipped as an unreadable raw JSON dump in all four lessons. Nothing in the executed check set (DOMAIN-SCHEMA-VALID, DOMAIN-VERIFIER, LAB-SCHEMA-VALID, RECEIPT-HASH-RESOLVES) verifies that this block is legible to the adult who must act on it or behaviourally consistent with the numbered steps above it.

function: Runs once per curriculum rather than per unit, over the set of units the run actually produced. Resolves every cross-unit reference -- next_lab_link targets above all -- against that set and fails on any target that does not exist; builds the prerequisite edge set from each unit's declared vocabulary and objectives and reports any concept a unit depends on that no earlier unit introduces; and runs cycle detection over the resulting graph. Deterministic graph operations, emitting a per-edge report; an LLM judge is used only for residual coherence questions the graph cannot answer.
what_makes_it_sota: K12-KGraph (arXiv:2605.09635) constructs a curriculum-aligned graph with seven node types and nine edge types including prerequisites_for, and validates it exactly this way: 'we run depth-first cycle detection on the is_a and prerequisites_for subgraphs and manually resolve any violations, yielding valid DAGs for the taxonomic and prerequisite relations.' The same paper's K12-Bench shows why the check must be deterministic rather than delegated: on its Prerequisite Reasoning task family, 'Prereq and Neighbor tasks are hardest... with EM below 35% even for Gemini-3-Flash', most models below 30% -- prerequisite reasoning is the weakest thing to ask a judge. SciEval (arXiv:2604.25472) scores instructional materials against the EQuIP rubric, whose design centre is coherence across a unit rather than the quality of a single lesson, establishing sequence-level review as standard practice. Sadhu & Dhor (arXiv:2512.22496) support evaluation at a different organisational level from per-unit review.
role_in_curriculum_builder: New curriculum-stage check in policy/checks.v1.yaml, running after all units in a run are generated and before the run is accepted -- a level at which this pipeline currently has no semantic check at all. It sits beside CUR-COUNT-DERIVED, which asserts how many units there should be; this one asserts that the units cohere with each other.
issues_resolved: A defect the QA report does not mention: L03/document/L03.md:112 sets next_lab_link to 'L05 asks you to plan a resistor's two connection points the same way this lab planned a wire's' and L04/document/L04.md:117 to 'L05 uses the same evidence-first habit to read a resistor's value', but outputs/arduino_kit_run_v2/ contains only L01-L04. Both are dangling forward references to a lesson that was never generated, each with a distinct invented description rather than repeated boilerplate. Relatedly, L04 teaches socket choice by expected current ('under 200 mA', 'above 200 mA') when no earlier unit in the sequence introduces current as a quantity. Every check in this run is per-unit, so no gate however strict could have caught either.
